# v0.1.3: verify the GCP content nodes behind api.anonrouter.ai

Since 2026-10-14 `api.anonrouter.ai` is served by Google Cloud Intel TDX content
nodes. 0.1.2 pins only the previous Phala deployment and fails closed against it.
This release verifies the new nodes in JavaScript and Python.

- Hop 1 for `api.anonrouter.ai` is held to the owner-signed release policy v3
  (`https://anonrouter.ai/.well-known/anonrouter-content-release-v3.json`),
  verified against owner public keys that ship in the package (owner root
  `10034ad2b11e9ef9f300da180a794010da369f2f14b2a896df42ceaf47077acb`, minimum
  sequence 6). No node image measurements ship, so a newly approved image needs
  no SDK release. Rollback, forks and revocation reversal are refused.
- Verification needs native DCAP, Intel `UpToDate` TCB, a fresh nonce and the
  TLS key read on the same socket that fetched the evidence: required connection
  binding, `verifyContentNode()` / `verify_content_node()`, or
  `anonrouter-verify gateway --dcap`. Unbound hop-1 calls against this origin now
  refuse with `unsupported_request` before any request.
- GCE machine identity (PZID) is verified when present and optional today.
- The backend's signed `tcbGrace` field is accepted; the SDK still requires
  `UpToDate`.
- `api.private.anonrouter.ai` (Phala rollback name) keeps its pin but is
  deprecated.

Upgrade guide: `docs/migrating-to-0.1.3.md`. Exact checks, live results and
limitations: `docs/release-readiness.md`. Before publication, the release
workflow installs the exact packed JavaScript and Python artifacts and requires
both to reach `hardware_verified` on `api.anonrouter.ai` with fresh nonces,
credential-free. No paid inference is implied.

The Python package is attached here as a wheel and sdist; it is not on PyPI.
`@anonrouter/client` is unchanged apart from its version.
